newsitem.title: USA: White House 'encouraged' by refugee move in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: White House 'encouraged' by refugee move in Zaire.

text.p: Reports that Rwandan refugees are streaming back toward their homeland from Zaire are "encouraging", the White House said on Friday as it pressed on with arrangements for possible participation in an international rescue force.

"That would be encouraging but it's very difficult to get an assessment on refugee flows there now ... The situation is still very complicated and our assessment continues," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.
"We are seeking assurances that the environment there would not present hostilities to any potential multinational force," McCurry told reporters at a briefing.
He said U.S. officials were working with "those we believe have influence" on militia groups in Zaire and Rwanda, in addition to having discussions with the governments in Kinshasa and Kigali.

White House National Security Adviser Tony Lake met in New York on Thursday with officials from countries likely to contribute troops to any multinational force sent to the area. McCurry said Lake was working closely with the Canadian government to put forward a U.N. resolution that would authorize a multinational force, and that the resolution could be unveiled later on Friday.

U.S. officials have said Washington had agreed in principle to send 1,000 troops to Goma, Zaire, to secure the airport and set up a protected corridor so refugees can return to Rwanda if they want to. They said another 3,000 U.S. troops would go to nearby countries to help arrange airlift for emergency supplies, if final agreements on the details and duration of the mission could be worked out.
